label: early original-phase step (t=3-5) after a k/z/2-initial prefix of consonants, current input i/m/n/d/v
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.026% of steps). About 90% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=3-5 (86% at t=3-4), mostly on the first occurrence of a token. It looks like a conjunction of distributed token evidence: the first token is k (15x lift; z and 2 also raise the rate), the preceding inputs come from {b,l,z,h,g,s,w} (prev_tok l 10x, prev2_tok b 13x), and the current input is i/m/n/d (4-7x). The strongest examples have prefixes like k b l followed by m or i. Magnitude is highest when every element matches (k b l [m]); the best predicate catches 70% of the top-activation quartile, against roughly 57% of the lowest quartile. Small spillover onto the <DEL> step and the first two copy steps (about 5% of mass each). Never fires at t=0-1 or at t>=7, and almost never after recall_idx 1. No clean boolean rule captures it: the best predicate reaches dev F1 about 0.23 (precision 0.17, recall 0.38), which suggests a thresholded sum of per-token contributions rather than a crisp category.
